hero.headline: Lucas Cardoso is a Product Designer at Elsevier
hero.sub: I design products for healthcare, enterprise SaaS, and AI-driven tools, environments where the interface has to hold up under real operational pressure.

about.heading: Where the work sits
about.body: With years of experience delivering products that impact millions of lives, I am always eager to learn, collaborate with diverse teams, and suggest improvements in products and processes. My goal is to design accessible, user-centered products that meet both customer needs and business objectives. I've worked in projects in healthcare, finance, advertising, marketing and customer support.

reporting-hub.headline: Helping healthcare organizations understand product adoption
reporting-hub.context: Reporting Hub aggregates analytics and usage reporting across Elsevier's clinical products, including ClinicalKey AI, into a single view for the people who have to answer for adoption and outcomes.
responsibilities: Interface and interaction design for dashboards and reporting views
Working alongside a Product Manager, Engineering, and a dedicated UX Researcher
Proposing research questions and discovery work beyond assigned tickets
highlights: Designed reusable reporting components adopted across multiple report types
Supported the migration to the Leyden Design System
Improved accessibility compliance through VPAT initiatives
Established dashboard patterns reused by later reporting products
reporting-hub.impact: Healthcare executives, medical directors, and account managers need to trust a number before they act on it. Most of the work is making that trust legible at a glance.

siga-emergencia.headline: Improving emergency care workflows for healthcare professionals
siga-emergencia.context: SIGA Emergência supports emergency departments and hospital operations at Hapvida, one of Brazil's largest healthcare providers. The work meant redesigning high-complexity clinical workflows, integrating multiple systems, and keeping the interface fast and trustworthy for professionals working under time pressure.
responsibilities: UX research and strategy for emergency and inpatient workflows
Maintaining the design system used across 12 healthcare products
Working directly with clinicians, developers, product managers, and stakeholders
highlights: Adopted in more than 800 medical units
Led emergency and inpatient experience initiatives end to end

carrefour.headline: Reducing customer support complexity across enterprise operations
carrefour.context: This project modernized Carrefour's customer support ecosystem by migrating operations to Salesforce Service Cloud, redesigning the workflows that service teams rely on for high-volume operations.
responsibilities: Product discovery and user flow mapping for agent-facing tools
Service and interaction design across more than 30 operational journeys
Running stakeholder workshops to align on scope and priorities
carrefour.impact: Agents were navigating a patchwork of legacy tools to resolve a single case. Most of the work was collapsing that into workflows that hold up at high volume.

interage.headline: Designing healthcare tools that support safer clinical decisions
interage.context: Interage is a healthcare platform focused on drug interaction analysis. The work centered on improving information architecture, search, and usability, so complex pharmaceutical information is easier to parse in the middle of a clinical decision.
responsibilities: Information architecture and interaction design for search and results
Usability improvements based on how professionals actually use the tool
Ongoing contributions to product evolution alongside the team
highlights: Improved navigation across complex medical information
Simplified access to critical clinical data during time-sensitive decisions
